item.title: Real Madrid summer signing becomes indispensable for Mourinho as veteran loses starting place
item.description: Real Madrid summer signing becomes indispensable for Mourinho as veteran loses starting place Ibrahima Konate has established himself as one of Jose Mourinho’s most trusted defenders since joining Real Madrid from Liverpool on a free transfer in the summer. Despite arriving after an inconsistent final season at Anfield, where he was targeted by fans and pundits, the French international has now become a regular starter alongside Dean Huijsen, making him an important figure in Mourinho’ss defensive structure. Statistically, his importance is reflected in his playing time, with Konate having accumulated 1,170 minutes this season, making him Real Madrid’s fourth-most-used outfield player behind Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde. Konate establishes himself alongside Dean Huijsen The partnership between Konate and Huijsen has provided Mourinho with a promising defensive combination. The Frenchman’s physical strength, recovery ability and effectiveness in one-on-one situations complement Huijsen’s composure and ability to initiate attacks from the back. Simply put, their contrasting qualities have helped establish a balance between defensive security and playing out from the back. Konate offers the aggression required to deal with opposition forwards, while Huijsen provides technical quality during the initial stages of possession, something that Virgil van Dijk does at Liverpool at times. Konate has become Mourinho’s dependable centre-back. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) For what it is worth, the French defender’s arrival had initially attracted questions because his performances at Liverpool had declined after winning the Premier League in 2024/25. His limited involvement for France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup also meant he arrived in Madrid without particularly strong recent momentum. It may very well be a blessing in disguise, as the lack of spotlight on his arrival seems to have made his life particularly easy for him. Mourinho’s selection decisions reveal Konate’s importance Konate started Real Madrid’s opening two La Liga matches against Espanyol and Real Sociedad before being rested against Malaga. He subsequently featured in every domestic league match, completing the full 90 minutes in each of his 13 starts across competitions. His involvement in the Champions League has been managed differently, with Mourinho rotating him for the fixtures against RB Leipzig and AEK Athens, which is understandable given that fixtures, both in club season and international breaks, are coming thick and fast. Konate’s rise has affected Antonio Rudiger’s game time at Real Madrid. item.description: David Warner was Test vice-captain at the time of the ball-tampering scandal [Getty Images] Usman Khawaja is "100% accurate" in his recounting of the Australia ball-tampering scandal in 2018, says former team-mate David Warner. Australia were found to have used sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Warner and captain Steve Smith were banned a year and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft for nine months. Khawaja last week said the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper, despite consistent denials from the bowlers that they had knowledge of the plan. Warner, who retired from international cricket in 2024, said in a video statement on Instagram: "It's been eight years since I spoke on this topic. And Ussie, I throw my full support behind you. "I thank you for what you've done. It's 100% accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth." Warner said the investigation process following the incident was "rushed and botched". item.title: Gauff opens WTA Finals with gritty win over Pegula
item.description: Coco Gauff is the number four seed at the WTA Finals [Getty Images] Coco Gauff battled to a three-set victory over fellow American Jessica Pegula as she made a winning start to the WTA Finals. Gauff, the 2024 champion, demonstrated resilience and superb athleticism to overcome 2023 runner-up Pegula 6-4 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 at Indian Wells in California. Gauff - at 22, the youngest player to appear at five consecutive WTA Finals since Martina Hingis in 2000 - last competed at the China Open in early October. "I'm really proud of myself for this one," she said. "To play a tournament like this with no preparation is something I've never done in my career, but I'm just really happy to get through. "It was a tough match. I was having a lot of fun." Gauff has won only one title this year, when she beat Pegula in the Cincinnati Open final in August. Pegula, 32, won titles in Dubai and Charleston and reached the semi-finals of the Australian Open and US Open. She is only four wins behind Elena Rybakina's tour-leading 54 this season, despite playing only one match since the US Open ended in September. "Jess is an incredible player. We always go back and forth," Gauff said. "Today the key was just trying to be aggressive, but I also had to run a lot. "My shoes are pretty torn up now. Some of my shoes are somewhere on the court there. So I'll have to change shoes tomorrow." WTA chair apologises to Pegula for airing of 'diva' comment Next Gauff will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, who beat Marta Kostyuk 6-2 6-4 in the opening match of the Finals. Pegula will take on Kostyuk. Czech 21-year-old Noskova won all four of her break points against Ukrainian Kostyuk, who was given a late call-up after world number one Rybakina withdrew on Saturday because of illness. The Finals features the top eight players this season and consists of two groups of four in a round-robin format. The top two from each group progress to the semi-finals, before the final on Sunday. Against Pegula, Gauff recovered from three break points down to hold for a 5-4 lead in the first set before breaking Pegula in the following game. Pegula won each of Gauff's first three service games in the second set as she raced into a 5-1 lead, but Gauff took the next three games. Pegula, who wasted three set points when serving at 5-4, unleashed a yell of frustration and slammed her racquet into the ground after missing two break points in the following game. Pegula survived match point on her own serve to force - then win - a tie-break. But Gauff dominated the deciding set, comfortably winning the first three games before converting a third match point and letting out an emotional roar. item.title: Atletico Madrid star Alex Baena explains what went wrong against Barcelona: ‘We didn’t give that 120%’
item.description: Atletico Madrid star Alex Baena explains what went wrong against Barcelona: ‘We didn’t give that 120%’ Atletico Madrid midfielder Alex Baena believes his side paid the price for losing intensity during the second half of their 2-1 defeat against Barcelona at the Metropolitano. The Spanish international felt Diego Simeone’s team had competed at the same level as Hansi Flick’s side during the opening period but admitted that Barcelona’s ability to punish even a slight drop in intensity ultimately proved decisive. Baena was particularly frustrated by Atletico’s lack of clinical finishing, arguing that his team created enough opportunities to get a better result. Baena explains why Atletico Madrid failed to beat Barcelona Atletico created several promising situations against Barcelona but struggled to convert their opportunities into goals. Baena acknowledged that his team had caused problems for the visitors, although their inefficiency in front of goal prevented them from taking greater advantage. “We caused them a lot of trouble, but we weren’t clinical in front of goal. We played a very good match. “Either side could have come away with the win, and this is a long season – this is the path we need to follow,” he began his assessment, according to AS . Baena admits Atletico Madrid’s intensity dropped in the second half. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Barcelona, on their part, showed greater efficiency in decisive moments, with Fermin Lopez scoring twice to complete the comeback. That difference proved particularly costly for Atletico given the opportunities Baena believed his team had created. Atletico’s intensity drops as Barcelona take control Baena identified the change in possession and intensity after half-time as a major reason behind Atletico’s inability to maintain their first-half performance. He argued that allowing Barcelona greater control of the ball inevitably makes life difficult against a team comfortable dominating possession. “When you let Barça have more possession, they take control of the match. We didn’t give that 120% we’d given in the first half, and when you drop to 100%, Barça dominate you. “We’ll try to keep giving 120 per cent for the full 90 minutes because that’s where the team needs to improve.” Barcelona were more clinical than Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Baena also returned to the issue of finishing when explaining the difference between the teams. “That was the difference: they had three or four chances and scored twice, whilst we had far too many and weren’t able to put one away. item.title: The Clippers finally closed one out, and the bench is the reason why
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) goes to the basket against New Orleans Pelicans forward/center Karlo Matkovic (17) during the first quarter at Intuit Dome. INGLEWOOD, Calif. – For the first time since opening night, the Clippers walked off the Intuit Dome floor on Sunday with a win, beating the New Orleans Pelicans 139-123 and putting an end to a seven-game losing streak that had dragged on for more than two weeks. It was also the first time in a while that a fourth quarter went their way, as the Clippers opened the final period on a 15-6 run to go up 117-101 and pushed the lead to as many as 20 after back-to-back games in which they let double-digit fourth-quarter leads get away. "It was good to get over the hump," Darius Garland said after the game. "Get that monkey off our back." How They Held On This Time The Clippers led by as many as 13 in the second quarter and took a 67-60 lead into halftime, but New Orleans opened the third on an 18-10 run and went up 78-77, which looked a lot like the stretches that had sunk them against Toronto and Miami. Ty Lue said he challenged the group in the timeout to stay with it, and Kobe Sanders hit a three with 2:23 left in the third that put the Clippers ahead 94-93 for good. "They're going to make a run," Lue said. "It's a game of runs." The bigger change was how they handled the ball, with the Clippers committing a season-low 11 turnovers after coming into the night averaging an NBA-worst 20.1 per game, while also handing out 34 assists and shooting a season-best 54.8% from the field. "Just sharing the basketball, attacking and making the right play," Lue said of the 34 assists. New Orleans got 26 points from Trey Murphy III, 25 from Jeremiah Fears and 25 from Zion Williamson, who went 9-of-9 from the field, but the Clippers had enough answers on the other end to keep the Pelicans at arm's length the rest of the way. item.title: USA & Pacifics to host 2030 Rugby League World Cup
item.description: The ongoing Rugby League World Cup is being held in Australia [Getty Images] The 2030 edition of the Rugby League World Cup will be held in the USA and the Pacific Islands. The five host cities are yet to be confirmed, but the men's and women's tournaments will run concurrently, as they are with this year's ongoing tournament which is being held in Australia. World governing body International Rugby League (IRL) said the aim was to expand the sport's reach to new countries. "This is a strategy to maximise the interest of broadcasters, government partners and fans in the current World Cup, which has regularly broken records for crowds and the number of television viewers," IRL chairman Tony Grant said at the board's annual general meeting (AGM) in Sydney. "At the same time we want to take advantage of opportunities that are opening up in new frontiers where the Rugby League World Cup hasn't previously been played." Grant also confirmed that the men's World Cup would expand from 10 teams to 12, while the women's event would consist of 10 instead of eight. The format of the tournament is yet to be decided after nations were asked for their feedback at the AGM, while the IRL has also proposed that Samoa and Tonga be promoted to Tier One nations alongside Australia, England and New Zealand. Samoa became the first Pacific country to play in a World Cup final in 2022, while they and Tonga both reached the semi-finals of this year's tournament. The 2030 Wheelchair World Cup will take place at the same time, but will be held in France, while the 2034 tournament will be hosted in Europe. Both men's and women's finals of the 2026 tournament are being contested between Australia and New Zealand, in Brisbane on Sunday 15 November. Australia's men have won the past three World Cups while their women are playing in their fifth successive final.

item.title: Sports Personality of the Year returns - with five awards decided by public
item.description: Gabby Logan, Alex Scott and Clare Balding will present the show [Getty Images] The 2026 BBC Sports Personality of the Year show will be held on Sunday, 13 December - with five winners decided by public votes. Clare Balding, Gabby Logan and Alex Scott will again host the programme, which will be hosted in Salford and broadcast live on BBC One, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app from 17:45 GMT. Five of the nine awards to be presented on the night will be decided by public vote. The show will celebrate another great year of sport, including Team GB's most successful Winter Olympics, England's best finish at a men's Fifa World Cup since 1966, and record-breaking displays at the European Athletics Championships. There will be two new award categories at the ceremony this year - Men's Footballer of the Year and BBC World Service Women's Footballer of the Year. The latter has been a BBC World Service award since 2015 but will now be presented as part of the BBC Sports Personality of the Year awards for the first time. Voting - for global audiences - opens on Tuesday, 10 November. In addition to crowning the winners of both football awards, fans will also select the winners of the World Sport Star of the Year, Team of the Year and Sports Personality of the Year award itself. An independent panel made up of industry experts, sports broadcasters, sports journalists and former sportspeople will determine the shortlists for the Sports Personality of the Year, Team of the Year and World Sports Star awards, with the winners chosen by public votes. The independent panel will also determine the winners of Young Sports Personality of the Year and Coach of the Year. Separate panels of football experts will provide the shortlist of contenders for Men's Footballer of the Year and Women's Footballer of the Year. Alex Kay-Jelski - director of BBC Sport - said: "What I love about BBC Sports Personality of the Year is that it brings together all those moments that stopped us in our tracks. The goals, the medals, the upsets, the records, the stories that had us talking at work, in the pub and around the dinner table. "And what a year we've had. This year's shortlists will be packed with athletes and teams who have achieved extraordinary things, but what's especially exciting is that audiences will have a bigger say than ever before in who takes home the trophies." The nine award categories are: BBC Sports Personality of the Year Helen Rollason Award Young Sports Personality of the Year Coach of the Year Team of the Year Lifetime Achievement award Men's Footballer of the Year Women's Footballer of the Year World Sport Star of the Year Full voting details, dates and T&Cs will be announced in due course.

item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - FEBRUARY 27: Toby Fournier #35 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts following her basket against the North Carolina Tar Heels during the first half at Cameron Indoor Stadium on February 27, 2025 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images D espite just getting Florida Atlantic on the schedule just 48 hours ago, Duke dominated the Owls, and particularly inside, en route to a 78-56 win. The margin there was 50-2, which is astonishing (and which points out that women’s basketball, while much improved, has not yet reached parity across the board). How dominant were the Blue Devils? Duke scored the majority of its points around the rim, and FAU was powerless to stop that. Duke also owned the boards, winning that battle 47-32, and converting 16 offensive rebounds into 22 second-chance points. The Blue Devils also forced 20 turnovers, and scored 21 points off of those turnovers. Finally, Duke got 41 points from its bench to support leading scorers Autumn Fleary (14 points and 4 assists), and Aaliyah Crump (13 points, 7 rebounds, 3 blocks, and 2 steals). And in the best news of the night, aside from the win itself, Toby Fournier returned from injury, racking up 10 points, 5 rebounds, 2 blocks, and 2 steals, in just 19 minutes. FAU wasn’t an imposing opponent, but it’s great that they were willing to accept this game on short notice, after Duke’s game against North Texas was canceled a few days ago. item.title: Stats behind Real Madrid superstar’s remarkable goalscoring streak amid sensational form
item.description: Stats behind Real Madrid superstar’s remarkable goalscoring streak amid sensational form Real Madrid’s excellent form in recent weeks has coincided with a red-hot scoring streak for Kylian Mbappe. The French striker has been scoring crucial goals game after game, helping put his team in a great position ahead of the November international break. According to Mundo Deportivo , Mbappe has scored in seven consecutive matches for Madrid, continuing his extraordinary form in the 3-0 victory over Valencia. Mbappe closing in on personal Real Madrid record The Frenchman scored Madrid’s third goal against Valencia, latching onto an excellent pass from Arda Guler before rounding the goalkeeper and finishing confidently. The strike extended his scoring streak to seven consecutive appearances, leaving him just one match away from equalling his personal best at Real Madrid. Mbappe previously scored in eight successive matches between September and October 2025, a record he now has within sight. Kylian Mbappe has been in a red-hot goalscoring streak. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The 27-year-old has been in sensational form this season, scoring 17 goals in just 16 appearances across all competitions. Thirteen have come in 12 La Liga matches, with Mbappe also scoring four in the Champions League. He sits second only to Raphinha in the Pichichi race. Mbappe has emerged as a key player for Mourinho and is one of the few who rarely get a rest. He has been instrumental in Real Madrid’s turnaround, and the team will hope his goalscoring streak continues after the break. Real Madrid’s growing dependence on Mbappe On the one hand, Mbappe’s growing goalscoring numbers are good to see. On the other, they also highlight Madrid’s overdependence on him for goals. Jude Bellingham is Los Blancos ‘ second-highest goalscorer this season, with just four goals to his name. Jose Mourinho needs to find goals from his team apart from Mbappe. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Madrid’s attack has thrived in recent matches, with the likes of Diomande and Guler becoming increasingly influential . However, in terms of goalscoring, none of the other attackers have been able to offer Mbappe enough support. The problem for Madrid is that this means Mourinho cannot risk leaving Mbappe out of the starting XI. As long as he continues to deliver with such astonishing consistency, Madrid have no concerns. It remains to be seen whether Mbappe can pick up where he left off when club football resumes.

item.title: Dutch match postponed after fans block team bus
item.description: Fans of Vitesse Arnhem celebrated an absence of away fans in the 2025-26 edition of their home match with De Graafschap [Getty Images] A Dutch second-tier match between Vitesse Arnhem and De Graafschap was called off after away team supporters blocked their own team's bus from departing for the game. Fans of De Graafschap were protesting the decision to ban away fans from attending the game at Vitesse's GelreDome stadium after supporters had not agreed to security measures set out for the derby fixture. Reports in Dutch media said De Graafschap fans gathered outside their stadium in Doetinchem early on Sunday and blocked the bus from leaving. The Dutch Football Association said in a statement that the match would not go ahead on Sunday and that the matter would be referred to the disciplinary bodies. "It is an unacceptable situation that the Vitesse - De Graafschap match cannot go ahead in this way. That supporters making football impossible is completely intolerable," it said. "In doing so, they harm their club, their team, the sport, and the thousands of supporters who do come for the football." In a Saturday statement , Vitesse announced that they had made the decision to ban away fans "based on police information and after extensive consultation with all involved security partners." They had proposed an away fans allocation of 500 - cut from the standard 800 - dependent on a number of security measures including "fan paraphernalia brought along had to be subject to inspection prior to the supporters' arrival." "Over the past few weeks, Vitesse, the police, and the municipality have repeatedly offered De Graafschap various options to meet these conditions. "However, police information and conversations with De Graafschap indicate that a portion of the supporters is insisting on bringing fan paraphernalia in a manner contrary to the agreements made." Vitesse added their decision had been made in light of "serious disturbances" surrounding the 2025-26 edition of the fixture, from which De Graafschap supporters were also banned. In their response to the announcement , De Graafschap said they did "not recognize the picture painted by the Arnhem press release regarding the commitment and stance of our club and our supporters. "As a club, we find it unacceptable that our supporters are portrayed in this manner." Responding to the cancellation Vitesse director Willem van der Linden said the cancellation was a "major disappointment". item.title: “Don’t have a clue what to do”: Gary Neville bemoans farcical leadership at club after Aston Villa draw
item.description: “Don’t have a clue what to do”: Gary Neville bemoans farcical leadership at club after Aston Villa draw Manchester United showed great spirit to twice come from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa. The match The side certainly has fight, having come from 0-2 down against AS Roma to win 3-2 in the Champions League last Tuesday. Nonetheless, there were more early goals conceded, and a complete lack of understanding of how to defend was once again publicly exposed at Old Trafford. A loss may have almost certainly sealed Michael Carrick ‘s fate, but with the fight shown in the final seconds of the game to snatch a draw, nobody is any the wiser as to what United’s board will decide over the international break regarding the manager’s future. Gary Neville on the ownership Speaking to NBC about where Manchester United stand after their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, the former captain of the club was once again less than impressed. Commenting on the possibility of changing manager, he claimed, “Michael Carrick did that last season – so you can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce. When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.” Neville added, “you can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer. Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.” The pundit lambasted years of poor decisions from the United board by stating, “it’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.” Neville asserted that none of it really mattered, though, as poor recruitment, poor performance departments, and a lack of leadership will crush any decent manager. He explained, “every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.” Finally, he claimed, “there are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.” United next play football on Sunday, 22nd November away to Liverpool, and it will be fascinating to see if Michael Carrick is still in the dugout. item.title: Steve Kerr Has Blunt Response to Kristaps Porzingis’ Decision to Step Away
item.description: The Golden State Warriors' season has thrown into chaos after the news that center Kristaps Porzingis will be stepping away from basketball after complications arose from postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, a nerve condition that kept Porzingis out of every regular season game this season and now will keep him off the court indefinitely. It's obviously devastating news for Porzingis, who will be facing an uncertain future as he works out how to address the condition, which affects an estimated 3-6 million Americans each year, with worldwide affliction rates not commonly known, but it also throws a wrench into the Warriors' system. Porzingis' absence happening so early into the regular season after the team had just signed him to a two-year, $40 million extension this offseason has left Golden State scrambling for a new center and until a true replacement is found in either free agency or the trade market, they'll be left with a mix of other players to fill the void. Head coach Steve Kerr was one of those figures and on the issue of Porzingis' announcement and illness, he spoke directly from the heart while struggling to find the right words to say himself. item.title: Capitals’ Tom Wilson Avoids Suspension After Controversial Hit
item.description: Tom Wilson talking to referee October 2026 Getty The Washington Capitals received surprising news on Sunday, as forward Tom Wilson will reportedly avoid further NHL discipline following his controversial hit on Florida Panthers defenseman Sandis Vilmanis. After receiving a five-minute major penalty and a game misconduct for boarding in Saturday’s 4-3 win over Florida, Wilson seemed likely to face additional punishment. However, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday morning that Wilson will not face added discipline for the play. Hearing no supplemental discipline for Tom Wilson — Elliotte Friedman (@FriedgeHNIC) November 8, 2026 The news comes as a surprise to most fans, with the Caps catching a break as they gear up for a challenging week. Wilson Avoiding Suspension Comes as Surprise It is no secret that Tom Wilson has faced discipline in the past, building a reputation as the Caps’ “bad boy” over his tenure. With a 20-game suspension in 2018, later reduced to 14 games on appeal, a seven-game suspension in 2021, and a six-game suspension as recently as 2024, Wilson doesn’t hold the best track record with the NHL’s Department of Player Safety. However, this time around, Wilson escaped with no further punishment and should be right back in action on Tuesday night against the Senators. The Panthers are still awaiting an update on Sandis Vilmanis, who just notched his first career two-goal game on Wednesday against Chicago. When asked for an update following Saturday’s game, Panthers head coach Paul Maurice shared that they were still waiting on any definitive news. “Getting looked at by another doctor,” Maurice said Saturday. “But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Capitals Week Ahead Nonetheless, with Wilson set to continue playing, Washington gears up for another important week, starting in Ottawa Tuesday before facing the Devils in back-to-back matchups to wrap up the week. Starting in Ottawa on Tuesday, the Senators currently sit 11-6-1 on the year and will face the Caps in their first of three games this season. The Caps and Ottawa have been tightly matched over the last few years, with the Capitals garnering a 4-3-3 record in their last 10 against the Senators. Following that matchup, the Caps will travel to New Jersey, where they will face off against the Devils on Thursday, then again at home on Saturday. Currently sitting below the Devils in the standings, the week provides a great chance for the Caps to build momentum off their Saturday win. With Wilson reportedly avoiding further discipline from the NHL’s Department of Player Safety, he will be ready alongside the Caps to help them climb the Metro standings, most likely skating a little calmer for a couple of games. item.title: Fishlock retires after record-breaking career
item.description: Jess Fishlock won more caps and scored more goals for Wales than any other player, male or female [Getty Images] Wales legend Jess Fishlock's playing career is over, after Seattle Reign were beaten 1-0 by Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off quarter-finals. The 39-year-old midfielder began her career with home town club Cardiff City in 2002. She played in eight different countries and collected Champions League winners medals with FFC Frankfurt and Olympique Lyonnais. Fishlock retired from international football in October 2025 after scoring 48 times in 166 international appearances - both Wales records. She won three NWSL Shields during a 14-season stint with Seattle but announced in April this season would be her last. "I've loved it," said an emotional Fishlock, as she wiped away tears after losing to Gotham on Sunday. "And the truth is I've loved that my last year was with this group, because they have just given me so much, and not just on the field." Fishlock will now be part of Rhian Wilkinson's Wales coaching staff for December's two-leg World Cup play-off against Norway. Wales face Denmark and Italy again on League A return Wales in fight to retain rising female stars Fishlock, who has previously held player-coach roles at Cardiff City Ladies and Melbourne Victory, joined Seattle for the inaugural NWSL season in 2013. Reign finished eighth in this year's regular season table to claim the final play-off berth, and they pushed number one seed Gotham close in a game during which Fishlock left the field in the 74th minute. "Two years ago I was just 'I can't work with these kids', as in I'm too old for it, but they have given me just so much joy," added Fishlock. "And obviously the older ones, we've just had to rely on each other so much these last couple of years and it's created deeper relationships within what we've already been doing, and because of that I've seen so much growth on and off the field from this team. "So even today I'm not upset that I'll never play football again - I'm ok with that, I've played enough - but I am devastated that I will not get to spend more time with this group because they will win." Reign defender Sofia Huerta said it had been a privelege to play with Fishlock, who she described as the best player she had ever seen. "She came into this league and it was so lucky to have her," said Huerta. "She put this league on the map. "Playing with Jess has been my greatest honour. I've seen her be the best professional, such a good player, but the best thing about Jess is she's just such a good person." item.title: Teenager Blades Brown becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in nearly 100 years
item.description: A 3-foot putt on the second playoff hole made Blades Brown the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years. The 19-year-old closed with a 9-under 63 to beat Ben James at the World Wide Technology Championship. “It hasn’t set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner,” Brown said. “I just go back to 5-year-old Blades that was watching the TV and watching Tiger Woods and all those great players win major championships, and to think that I’m now in a similar spot with having won a PGA Tour event is mind-blowing.” Brown decided to turn professional just two years ago, while still a junior in high school. No-one younger has won since Charles Kocsis, who was 18 when he took the Michigan Open in 1931, an event considered regional in the early years of the PGA. Blades Brown turned professional during his junior year of high school (Getty) James had led by four going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante, and lost that advantage. His response showed moxie: he smoked a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and made eagle, salvaging a 70 and forcing a playoff. “Had a feeling that it was going to go in,” James said of his clutch eagle, the only putt he made all day longer than 15 feet. “Hadn’t really made anything all day. Just had a really good line on it and it was a good putt. Played the best I could.” The second extra hole settled it, as James missed from 8 feet and Brown holed his 3-footer. James was the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking last season. Brown earned his PGA Tour card this year through a place among the top 20 in Korn Ferry Tour points. Ben James chips onto the 18th green during the second playoff hole (Getty) For a sleepy FedEx Cup Fall event on the southern tip of Baja California, it amounted to a tense playoff between two players from the next generation. Brown's final round had already erased a seven-shot deficit. The wait tested him further, as he went through two bags of golf balls on the range to see whether his two-shot lead over James would hold. Then came a return to the par-5 18th for the playoff. Their approach shots on the first extra hole finished side-by-side, about 3 feet apart, and both narrowly missed eagle chances. They went back to the 18th tee, where their drives ended up next to each other, and both came up just short of the green. James watched his pitch nearly drop before it ran out 8 feet. Brown had hit a similar pitch in regulation to 6 feet for a closing birdie, but this time came up 3 feet short. Blades Brown and Ben James shake hands on the 18th green (Getty) James' birdie attempt grazed the right edge, and Brown poured in the winner. “I’m so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways,” Brown said. “I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it and I can’t wait for what’s next.” Eight players had been separated by two shots on the back nine.
